memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Abraham looked up and there in a thicket he saw a ram caught by its horns. He went over and took the ram and sacrificed it as a burnt offering instead of his son. - Gen 22:13 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Abraham looks up and sees it: a ram, caught in a thicket, provided by God at the perfect moment. And he offers it "as a burnt offering instead of his son." That word - instead - is one of the most important words in the whole Bible. The ram died in Isaac's place. A substitute took the death that Isaac deserved to die.

This is the great principle of substitution, and it runs all the way through Scripture to the cross. Isaac lay on the altar under the sentence of death; the ram died in his place; Isaac walked free. A life was given so that another could live. This is exactly the pattern of our salvation.

For we too were under the sentence of death because of our sin. And God provided a Substitute - not a ram, but His own Son. Jesus took the death we deserved. "He himself bore our sins in his body on the tree" (1 Pet 2:24). Like Isaac, we walk free - not because the penalty was cancelled, but because Another bore it in our place.

Notice that God provided the substitute. Abraham did not find the ram by his own effort; God supplied it. In the same way, we could never provide our own salvation. God Himself gave the sacrifice that saves us. When you consider your standing before God, remember the ram in the thicket - and the greater Substitute it pointed to. Jesus died instead of you, so that you might go free.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Do you grasp that Jesus died "instead of" you, as your substitute?
- Have you received the freedom that comes from the sacrifice God provided?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, thank You for the substitute in the thicket, and for the greater Substitute it pointed to. Thank You that Jesus took the death I deserved, so I could walk free. I receive Your salvation with a grateful heart.
Amen.
